- Slack notification workflows and chat automations align with established international system standards.

Spain Operations and Business Rules
- Hartman and Hertz integrations project 200 to 400 transports per week locally.
- Initial transports generate heavy support demand during a 2-hour window as drivers learn the app.
- Juliana requires Spain-specific legal regulations, business rules, and client contracts to configure custom workflows.
- Artur schedules a meeting with Danny to identify unmapped operational challenges in Spain.

AI Deployment Timeline and Contingency Plan
- Thiago estimated a 4 to 6-week development window for the AI chat feature on October 15.
- Targeting an AI launch by the end of next month, pending sprint schedule confirmation.
- Management will hire a local area manager if the AI deployment misses the customer launch window.

Decisions

Aligned
- Replication of regional infrastructure for Spain: The participants aligned on utilizing the same HubSpot, Livia, and Slack notification infrastructure in Spain that was established for Brazil and Mexico.

Details
AI Knowledge Base Status: Artur Morais initiated a discussion regarding support helping with standard operating procedures and artificial intelligence. Juliana Coelho stated that they finished the artificial intelligence knowledge base for configurations and planned to send the link to the team. Furthermore, Juliana Coelho mentioned that they talked to Chiago and Edu from the artificial intelligence team to ensure everything was functioning properly. Artur Morais noted that they were waiting for this implementation and suggested having a conversation with Danny later to address Spain operations, yard specifics, and unmapped problems.

Business Rules and Documentation for Spain Operations: Juliana Coelho requested that the team send any existing documentation, legal specifics, and business rules related to Spain to help them understand local procedures and client contexts similar to the United States setup. Juliana Coelho also emphasized the importance of receiving contracts and rules for specific clients like Kavak and Pinsky to handle distinct cases such as dry runs for area managers directly versus routing them to support. Artur Morais agreed to review what they had so far and scheduled a follow-up meeting with Danny in Spain to map out complex, unmapped problems.

Spain Transport Challenges and Volume Projections: Artur Morais explained that initial transport services in Spain required a disproportionately higher amount of problem-solving compared to Latin America, Mexico, and Brazil because most transports involved new drivers and customers. These drivers were accustomed to competitor applications and required assistance with basic confirmations and finding plates within a concentrated two-hour window. Armando Flores and Artur Morais highlighted that upcoming large customer closures, including Hartman and Hertz, would push local transport volume to between 200 and 400 transports per week via Flexiart. Armando Flores stated that if the artificial intelligence could not resolve these initial support needs, they would be forced to hire an area manager locally to handle escalations at level two.

Technical Infrastructure and HubSpot Integration: Juliana Coelho explained that the artificial intelligence voice and live chat systems would be fully synchronized with HubSpot, allowing tickets created by the artificial intelligence to route directly into HubSpot and data to be reviewed via SuperSet. Artur Morais asked if Slack notifications and channels could be built similarly, and Juliana Coelho confirmed that they would maintain the same overall infrastructure as used in Brazil and Mexico. Dan Rizzo later clarified with Armando Flores that the system involved the artificial intelligence hooking up through WhatsApp and a new Salesforce instance.

Implementation Timeline Estimates: Artur Morais recalled that the last update from Thiago on October 15 estimated a timeline of four to six weeks to launch the artificial intelligence chat feature, projecting a worst-case scenario completion by the end of next month. Artur Morais pressed for specific dates, but Juliana Coelho stated that they could not provide a hard completion date without first checking Thiago's sprint. Dan Rizzo asked Juliana Coelho if they had spoken to Thiago regarding whether the implementation would be straightforward, to which Juliana Coelho reiterated that feasibility depended on current requirements and sprint capacity, promising to consult with Thiago to determine what could be achieved on time.
